Understanding recursion in programming

Recursion is a technique in which a function calls itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem.

Every recursive function needs a base case, because without it the call stack would keep growing until the program crashes.

A classic example is computing the factorial of a number, where n factorial equals n multiplied by the factorial of n minus one.
